sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: ELISA on intact (non-permeabilized) HEK293A cells confirmed surface-accessible FLAG signal, demonstrating correct membrane trafficking; receptor activation studies (L1/L2) confirmed functional agonist responses from the FLAG-tagged construct.
sites.rationale: GPR35 has no signal peptide (topology landmarks show EXTRACELLULAR 1–20, not SIGNAL); the N-terminus is therefore constitutively extracellular and a prepend tag (insert_after_residue=0) sits on the cell surface. Python confirms residue 1 is M and the extracellular span extends 20 residues before TM1 begins at residue 21, placing the junction well beyond the ≥3-residue TM-clearance requirement. L6 is the strongest evidence because it explicitly uses intact (non-permeabilized) cells for ELISA, directly demonstrating surface accessibility of the FLAG tag; L1, L2, and L5 corroborate with functional receptor assays using the same N-terminal FLAG architecture. Because no paper names a specific residue number for the junction (only 'N-terminal'), position_evidence is topology_derived: the extracellular N-terminus is the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag. N-terminally FLAG-tagged GPR35 short and long isoforms expressed in HEK293A cells; surface expression quantified by ELISA on intact (non-permeabilized) cells. The same N-terminal FLAG prepend architecture is independently reported in L1 (NanoBiT vector, β-arrestin2 recruitment) and L2 (pcDNA vector, receptor activation studies), and in the FLAG-hGPR35a-eYFP construct of L5.

sources.claim: Prior to pharmacologically characterizing the GPR35 isoforms, we first quantified the expression levels of N-terminally FLAG-tagged GPR35 short and long, which only differ by a 31 amino acid long extension ( Fig. 2 A ), on the surface of HEK293A cells by performing ELISA experiments with intact cells ( Figs. 2 B and S1 ).

literature_notes: All C-terminal tags in the ledger (LgBiT in L1/L2, HA in L3/L4, eYFP in L5/L7/L8, GFP/EGFP in L9/L10/L11) are attached after residue 309, which falls in the intracellular C-terminal tail (topology landmarks: INTRACELLULAR 280–309). None qualifies as a surface tag site. L4 (anti-HA probing) was examined carefully: the quote does not specify non-permeabilized cells, and the C-terminus is topologically intracellular, so this cannot be read as surface detection of the HA tag. L8 names five phospho-acceptor residues (Ser287, Ser294, Ser300, Ser303, Thr307) in the intracellular C-terminal tail; four of the five alanine substitutions reduced BRET signals and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports any insertion in ECL1 (78–87), ECL2 (155–169), or ECL3 (240–256), so no internal extracellular loop sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: Ser287Ala in the intracellular C-terminal tail of hGPR35a-eYFP reduced maximal zaprinast-stimulated BRET signal, indicating this residue contributes to arrestin-recruitment signalling.
Ser294Ala in the intracellular C-terminal tail did NOT reduce BRET signal; position is intracellular and not function-perturbing by this assay.
Ser300Ala in the intracellular C-terminal tail of hGPR35a-eYFP reduced maximal zaprinast-stimulated BRET signal.
Ser303Ala in the intracellular C-terminal tail of hGPR35a-eYFP reduced maximal zaprinast-stimulated BRET signal.
Thr307Ala in the intracellular C-terminal tail of hGPR35a-eYFP reduced maximal zaprinast-stimulated BRET signal.
